summary: Replan on an amended spec, against a branch that already carries an implementation. Commit 771451a shipped ClientMembership, RequestNotification, the principal, the contacts routes, client-addressed requests, the notification port, the client shell and the cases; the review then blocked and a person amended the spec, adding REQ-03-043 and TC-03-INT-36 — a contacts read of its own for the new-request modal, guarded by `create-request` rather than `view-clients`, bounded by the projects the requester is assigned to. So this pass is a delta on a working tree, not a build from zero. Five pieces: (1) the new route GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/request-contacts and the modal reading it instead of the clients + per-client-contacts loop; (2) the reassign trail — an assignee_changed event whose oldValue/oldLabel are null when the outgoing addressee was a contact, against spec 01 requirement 35 and this spec's contracts; (3) one client-principal route gate in the org layout, so no staff screen renders behind a typed address — the members screen is the one that does today; (4) TC-03-E2E-03's two hand-built browser contexts, which carry no baseURL and throw on the first relative goto; (5) TC-03-UNIT-02, which asserts a normalized role where the case names the absent one. Every other task below is unchanged and is recorded so the plan still accounts for the whole spec — the implementer touches a task marked `state: shipped` only if this pass's delta names it.

tasks.changesThisPass: One defect, at reassignRequest. Spec 01 requirement 35 says reassignment writes an assignee_changed event 'carrying the old and new display names in oldLabel / newLabel, so the trail stays readable after a member is removed', and this spec's contracts say 'Display names keep being snapshotted into the event's label columns, so the trail survives a removed contact'. The `previous` lookup reads locked.assigneeMembershipId only, so reassigning a CLIENT-addressed request to a member writes oldValue: null and oldLabel: null — the request leaves the contact's inbox naming nobody it was taken from. Fix: when locked.assigneeKind === 'client' and locked.assigneeClientMembershipId is set, read that ClientMembership inside the same transaction (select the account's firstName/lastName) and write oldValue = the client-membership id, oldLabel = displayNameOf(account). The route's own answers do not change: the BODY still accepts only assigneeKind 'member' (a body naming a contact stays 400 REQUEST_MESSAGES.assigneeInvalid), and clearing assigneeClientMembershipId on the update stays, so exactly one half of the addressee is ever set. Also correct the two comments that now say something false: the one at the top of reassignRequest, which reads as though the whole route refused a client-addressed row, and the one beside the inactive-addressee banner in T7's file, which asserts 'this release has no reassign path that accepts a client addressee' next to a control that is drawn and works. Say what is true: the reassign body takes a colleague, and a client-addressed request may be handed to one — with the outgoing contact snapshotted into the event.

tasks.changesThisPass: The gate REQ-03-019 needs on the web side, and it goes in ONE place. Today the staff screens short-circuit unevenly: projects calls notFound(), clients returns null, documents/settings/time-tracking all gate on a role-keyed helper that answers false for a null role — and the members screen has no gate at all, because every staff role may see it. A contact who types /org/{orgId}/members is therefore served the page header, the search field and the show-removed checkbox over a skeleton that never resolves, since the members read answers them 404 and the non-ok branch leaves `members` null. Add the gate to apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/layout.tsx, where the principal is already resolved: once the session is ready, a principal of kind `client` on any path other than the requests destination calls notFound(). Allow exactly `/org/{orgId}/requests` and paths under `/org/{orgId}/requests/`; use usePathname(). One mechanism at the class of call sites beats nineteen page-level gates, and it is what makes 'a destination the caller cannot use is neither drawn nor reachable by typing' true for screens nobody has written yet. While in members/page.tsx, correct the comment added there — it asserts 'A client contact never reaches this screen (REQ-03-019)', which is the claim the gate is now making true rather than an observation about the code as it stood.
